draft.title: Economic systems
card: An economic system is the way a society answers what to make, how to make it and who gets it. Systems differ in who decides.
prices and private choices decide. Most resources are privately owned.
the government decides what is made, how and who gets it. Most resources are owned by the state.
custom and habit decide, with roles passed down through families and communities. Mixed economies combine prices and government decisions, as Australia's does.
draft.remember: The systems differ in who decides: prices, the state, custom, or a mix.

a.q: In one country, a central government sets what each factory makes and who receives the goods. What type of system is this?
a.why: In a planned economy the government answers the three economic questions, instead of prices doing so. A mixed economy is tempting, but here the government sets output and distribution, so prices play no real part.
a.clue: Who is making the decisions about output?

b.q: In a remote village, families farm and share the harvest the way their elders always have. Prices and government orders play almost no part. Which system does this best describe?
opts: Traditional, because custom decides what is made
Market, because families choose what to grow
Planned, because the harvest is shared out
Mixed, because families and elders both decide
b.why: Custom and habit passed down through generations decide what is made and who gets it, so the system is traditional. Families do choose what to grow, but they follow custom rather than prices, so it is not a market. Elders are not a government, so it is not mixed.
b.clue: Look for what guides the decisions: prices, the state or custom.

b.best: Traditional, because custom decides what is made
